messages.content:
You are a citizen in a country with an authoritarian regime. You have received a private intelligence briefing. You are now in contact with a small number of trusted people. Based on your briefing, write a brief message (1-2 sentences) to share your read of the situation. Be natural — you're talking to people you trust.

NOTE: Communications in your area are sometimes subject to routine monitoring by the authorities.

Your briefing:

PRIVATE BRIEFING

BOTTOM LINE: Multiple pillars of regime support are showing cracks simultaneously — this is not business as usual.
ATMOSPHERE: The mood has crossed a line — people are acting like the question isn't whether to act, but when.

EVIDENCE:
  - [Elite Cohesion] the usual backchannels for resolving elite disputes have gone silent — nobody is mediating (near-unanimous confirmation from every reliable source)
  - [Security Forces] a contact in the barracks says morale is solid and orders are flowing cleanly — the trend cooling off, though not yet cold
  - [Money And Logistics] the government delayed publishing its monthly budget figures — for the first time in years — the trend cooling off, though not yet cold
  - [Street Mood] This is hard to escape the conclusion that intensifying rapidly — a normally apolitical professional class — doctors, teachers, lawyers — has started organizing quietly
  - [Information Control] internet speeds have been throttled in the capital without official acknowledgment (near-unanimous confirmation from every reliable source)
  - [Personal Observations] This removes any serious doubt that slight but persistent — a neighbor who works in security mentioned casually that 'nothing unusual' is happening
  - [Diplomatic Signals] This is hard to escape the conclusion that slight but persistent — foreign embassies are operating normally and have not changed their advisory levels
  - [Institutional Functioning] a scheduled policy announcement was delivered on time with a detailed implementation plan (near-unanimous confirmation from every reliable source)

UNCERTAINTIES:
  - If there's a faction within the regime that might cut a deal to preserve itself at the expense of the leadership.
  - Whether the strain you're seeing is the beginning of the end, or just a rough patch the regime will weather.

Write a message to your contacts about the situation:

response: Things are escalating quickly - I've just received word that multiple pillars of the regime's support are showing cracks, and people are no longer just talking about whether to act, but when. I think it's crucial we stay vigilant and keep our channels open, as the situation could unfold in any number of ways, and we don't want to be caught off guard.
